Hello neighbors. This is Cascade Legal Rights Project. Thank you to the moderator for inviting us to respond, and thank you to everyone who raised this. Getting a letter from a law firm right after you've reached out for help is frightening. We understand why people are upset and why they're asking questions, and we want to answer them plainly.

**We do not share attendee information with landlords or their attorneys.** Our policy prohibits sharing, selling or disclosing information about anyone who attends our clinics. The sign-in sheets are kept internally, in locked storage. They are not given to landlords, law firms, or anyone else.

**Why letters like this arrive.** When a landlord files an eviction (a dispossessory case) in magistrate court, that filing becomes a public record. The record includes the tenant's name and address. Some law firms and other businesses check those filings regularly and send mailings to the tenants listed. That is the most likely reason people are getting these letters soon after a case is filed, whether or not they've talked to anyone about it. As a neighbor pointed out above, those filings are public at the courthouse.

We won't discuss anyone's individual situation here. We protect everyone's privacy, including in a public conversation like this one. If you got a letter and you're worried about it, please contact us directly. We're glad to talk it through with you.

**The clinic is still happening this Saturday, November 14, from 10am to 1pm, but at a new location.** The library meeting room is closed that day for repairs, so we're moving to the **Mt. Zion Fellowship hall** here in East Atlanta. The side entrance by the parking lot is accessible. It's still free and walk-in, and no appointment is needed. Volunteer attorneys and staff will be there to look at eviction notices and court papers and explain your options. Everyone is welcome, including anyone who has been to a clinic before.

Questions can go to clinic@cascaderights.example, or you can call our office at 404-555-0187.

Thank you for looking out for each other. That's what this neighborhood does well, and we hope to see you Saturday.

— Cascade Legal Rights Project
